physdesc.extent: 3 boxes (2 letter document boxes and 1 oversize document box)

userestrict.p: The Rockefeller Archive Center has title, copyright, and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them, and has authority to grant permission to cite and publish archival material from the collection.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains correspondence, articles, photographs, and ephemera related to Frederick "Fred" and Carrie Midgley's work on the island of Syros (Syra) in Greece as part of Near East Relief.

The bulk of the collection is a scrapbook and letters describing the journey to Greece, their work at the orphanage, and the trip home. The letters in the collection were primarily written by Carrie Midgley and sent to their son, William Bancroft Midgley, who transcribed them. The collection also contains medals and certificates honoring their service to Near East Relief.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Frederick "Fred" Midgley was born in 1865 in London, and he moved with his family to Worcester, Massachusetts in 1869. Carrie Bancroft Midgley was born on August 2, 1867, in Worcester, Massachusetts.

Fred worked for the American Steel and Wire Co., but he left this role to pursue dairy and poultry farming. In 1883, he joined the Worcester Grange and pursued leadership positions in the organization later in life.

The Midgleys married on May 30, 1887. They started a market garden in the Blithewood section of Worcester where they lived with their children, Bertha (Midgley) Winters, Mildred (Midgley) Pierce, Lorey G. Midgley, Harold A. Midgley, William B. Midgley, and Frederick Midgley, Jr.
Fred Midgley served as a member of the Worcester City Council from 1907-1910.

In August 1926, Fred became a member of the Overseas Staff with Near East Relief (NER) and signed a contract for two years. Dr. Arthur W. Gilbert, the Massachusetts commissioner of agriculture, recommended Fred for the position based on his experience teaching agricultural practices to young workers from diverse backgrounds on his farm, the expertise demonstrated in the Midgley's own market garden, and his leadership experience in agricultural organizations.

From 1926-1928, the Midgleys developed a farm at the orphanage on the island of Syra (Syros, Greece), taught farming techniques, and helped to care for the 1,400 children housed there. With support from NER and the Grange, the initial farm setup included Fred's own blight-proof celery, apples, pears, grapes, raspberries, gooseberries, currants, peonies, roses, a flock of chickens, pigs, and cattle.
After their service in Near East Relief, the couple returned to their farm in Worcester. Frederick Midgley died in 1949, and Carrie Midgley died in 1953.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Original order, as received. Files and file structure authenticated and preserved.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: The Near East Foundation records, Special Collections, Fred and Carrie Midgley papers were transferred to RAC in 2012 and ingested by RAC as Accession 2012:071.

did.unittitle: Near East Foundation records, Fred and Carrie Midgley papers

physdesc.extent: 3 boxes (2 letter document boxes and 1 oversize document box)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Reference documents written by Nancy Winter Taylor, Fred and Carrie Midgely's granddaughter. Includes description of materials in collection and list of family members.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Orphans, interiors and exteriors of buildings, Syra Institution of Vocational Training for Delinquent and Abandoned Children. Some photographs appear to be duplicates with captions in the scrapbook material.

did.unittitle: Volume I - Scrapbook - Correspondence, Articles, and Photographs

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Work contract with Near East Relief, correspondence with Near East Relief written prior to the Midgleys' departure on September 16, 1926, articles about the Midgleys' and their work, photographs and ephemera from the S.S. Braga, photographs of orphans, landscape, house, and farming in Syra, Greece, small American flag made and given to the Midgley's by a girl in the hospital, photographs of family visiting the Midgleys, photographs of distribution of 2000 St. Louis dolls to Armenian orphans, handwritten music books and lyrics for chapel services

did.unittitle: Volume II - Transcribed Letters Written by Carrie and Fred Midgley (p. 1-334)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Letters sent to Fred and Carrie Midgley's son, William Bancroft Midgley, who transcribed them into their current form. The letters were primarily written by Carrie and contained details on their trip to Greece, time in Syra, Greece, visit to Constantinople with family, and their trip home through Athens, Orient Express to Venice through Milan, Domodossola, Montreux, Geneva, Paris, Calais, Belgrade, and London (arrived June 1928). They left from Southhampton, England on the Leviathan on June 24, 1928 to Cherbourg, France and then New York.

did.unittitle: Correspondence and Articles - Return from Greece

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Letters from friends and family upon return to United States, articles about work and awards received, correspondence from 1950 with woman from Greece regarding Fred Midgley's death, stamp collection, and photocopy of Frederick Midgley's obituary from 1949

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: One Near East Relief service medal and two other small Near East Relief medals
